title: The expected NMDA-receptor decay time of local neurons did not predict spiking timescales across 179 mouse brain regions (IBL autocorrelograms, Allen MERFISH and 10x atlas)
abstract: Question: network models give long intrinsic timescales from slow NMDA-receptor currents. GluN2 subunits set the decay time (2A about 50 ms, 2B and 2C about 300 ms, 2D about 2 s). Does the GluN2 mix of local neurons predict the spiking timescale of mouse brain regions? Data: 56,610 IBL Brain-Wide Map units in 179 regions; timescale tau from exponential fits to whole-recording autocorrelograms (0.02-1.94 s). Region expression is Allen MERFISH neuron-type composition multiplied by 10x type means; Zhuang-ABCA-1 is the replication. The plan was frozen before any structure-to-timescale statistic. Results: the kinetic score (expression-weighted GluN2 decay time) had Spearman rho -0.05 with log tau (planned positive; spatial-surrogate p = 0.58; random-gene p = 0.56). Inside divisions the partial rho was +0.09 (p = 0.097); with rate and coordinates +0.06 (p = 0.19). The replication brain gave -0.09 and a per-unit estimator 0.00. A larger GluN2B share went with shorter tau (-0.37), against the prediction, but no subunit link passed the spatial null. Grin1 expression, Pvalb neuron share and Knox self-connection density also did not predict tau. Exploratory: the tau map was reliable (split-half 0.58), and 20 transcriptome PCs predicted held-out spatial blocks (CV R2 0.32 vs 0.18 for geometry), but the NMDA features added nothing, and 163 receptor and channel genes did not beat random gene sets (p = 0.35). In 42 cortical areas the kinetic score had rho +0.45, but not beyond a cortical spatial null (p = 0.076) or after layer control. Limitations: the aggregate autocorrelogram includes the task; mRNA, not receptor protein; region averages; only effects above about rho 0.43 could pass the spatial null.

citations.reason: We reuse its region-expression code (MERFISH x 10x), data recipe and null design, and apply them to a receptor-kinetics hypothesis for timescales.

Cortical hierarchy did not reliably predict timescales; layer sampling was a confound. Our brain-wide and isocortex tests of a molecular predictor also find no robust link, and we confirm longer deep-layer timescales.
Region and unit rules for IBL units come from this work (via 8811fcd1).
